subject: Uptime guardrails & pricing escalation — request for premium path and remedies
messages:
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
From: Ava Lind <ava.lind@fluxbank.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: platform@fluxbank.com
Subject: Production latency tail and availability incidents this week — need options

Soojin,

We saw repeated tail-latency spikes and two short availability blips on Tuesday and Wednesday that affected our fraud scoring pipeline. The SDK/reporting points to token-timeouts and elevated queueing on the hosted endpoint (model: rdl-ggml-22B-quant). Our SREs are asking for options: a clear SLA for uptime/latency, a path to prioritized capacity (dedicated or premium routing), and a way to get remediation credits if this recurs.

We have a renewal conversation next month, and this incident has raised the risk of us moving to a self-hosted approach unless we can secure guardrails. Can we get a concrete proposal by EOD Friday?

Thanks,
Ava Lind
Head of Platform, FluxBank

(attachments: fluxbank-incident-timeline-20261109.csv)

Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: Ava Lind <ava.lind@fluxbank.com>
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Subject: Re: Production latency tail and availability incidents this week — need options

Hi Ava — thanks for the heads up and for the timeline. I’m really sorry this interrupted your pipeline. We’re pulling logs and tracing the requests that saw elevated queueing.

Immediate next steps I’m taking:
- Sean will run a capacity sweep on your dedicated/hosted routing for the last 72 hours to confirm contention sources.
- Karthisk (cc’d) will check our kernel selection and batching heuristics for rdl-ggml-22B-quant on the host pool you use.
- I’ll prepare a short proposal: (1) an expedited premium routing pilot (24/7 reserved slices), (2) explicit latency SLOs for the pilot, and (3) a remediation credit framework if the SLOs are missed.

Can you confirm whether FluxBank is comfortable with a 3-month pilot (commit + usage) if we can meet the SLO? That will help the commercial terms.

— Soojin
So in Lee
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
(attachment: —)

Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:20:00 -0800
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Ava Lind <ava.lind@fluxbank.com>
Subject: Re: Production latency tail and availability incidents this week — need options

On Tue, Nov 10, 2026 at 10:05 AM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Immediate next steps I’m taking:
> - Sean will run a capacity sweep on your dedicated/hosted routing for the last 72 hours to confirm contention sources.

I pulled the request traces. Quick notes:
- The majority of affected requests line up with a sudden burst from a third-party enrichment service between 13:05–13:18 UTC on 2026-11-09 which increased average seq-lens by ~45%. Our autoscaler lagged on that specific pool because of fragmentation across shards.
- No single host OOM; instead we saw elevated queue times as micro-batches waited for available GPU slots.

I think a two-part mitigation is best: 1) short-term: move FluxBank to a reserved micro-slice with pre-warmed workers (reduces cold-start/queue lag), 2) medium-term: add a routing rule that routes high-priority tokens to a low-batch lane when sequence length variance spikes.

I’ll attach the raw trace CSV — it correlates with Ava’s timeline.

— Sean
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: fluxbank-traces-20261109.csv)

Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 08:34:00 -08:00
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: Ava Lind <ava.lind@fluxbank.com>, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Subject: Proposed technical guardrails and SLOs for pilot

Hi all,

I reviewed the model profile and the recent kernels selected for rdl-ggml-22B-quant. Proposal for the premium pilot:
- Dedicated micro-slice: 6 pre-warmed workers per region (us-west, us-east) with a max-batch size cap of 8 for the lane.
- Latency SLO (p99 generate): <= 420ms for <= 2048 tokens; availability SLO: 99.95% monthly
- Fallback policy: automatic throttled-batch mode when avg seq-length > 1500 to keep tail latency bounded
- Credit policy: for any month where p99 > SLO for more than one day, FluxBank receives a service credit equal to 10% of that month’s usage for the affected route (capped at 30%).

I’ll put this into a draft PDF and share with commercial. If FluxBank wants to escalate availability SLO to 99.98% we should discuss reserved capacity and a longer commit.

— Karthisk (Karthik Iyer)
Applied ML / Serving Optimization, Redwood Inference
(attachment: proposed-premium-path-draft-20261114.pdf)

Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 12:07:00 -08:00
From: Ava Lind <ava.lind@fluxbank.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Subject: Re: Proposed technical guardrails and SLOs for pilot

Soojin — thanks for the quick turnaround and for the concrete numbers. The SRE team reviewed the draft and had two asks: 1) can the p99 be tightened to 350ms for critical fraud-scoring routes (we’ll identify two route IDs), and 2) we need a runbook for post-incident customer escalation with staffing contacts for weekend coverage.

FluxBank is open to a 3-month pilot with a commercial commit if those two items are satisfied. The credit framework looks reasonable. We’ll redline the PDF and return by COB Monday.

Best,
Ava
(attachments: fluxbank-sre-comments-20261113.pdf)

Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 18:05:00 -08:00
From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: Ava Lind <ava.lind@fluxbank.com>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Subject: Re: Proposed technical guardrails and SLOs for pilot — commercial terms

Ava — appreciate the specificity from your SREs. Quick commercial reply while we incorporate the two asks into the pilot doc:

- We can commit to a targeted p99 of 350ms for the two named fraud-scoring routes. To achieve this we’ll provision a slightly larger reserved micro-slice and a dedicated low-batch lane for those routes.
- We’ll provide a weekend escalation runbook and a named on-call contact list (primary + secondary) for the pilot window.
- Commercial terms: 3-month pilot, committed monthly spend of $35k/month for the reserved micro-slice across both regions; standard usage billed above that. If SLO misses occur per the credit policy, we’ll apply credits to the following invoice.

Next step: Ava, if you can return the redlines and confirm the two route IDs by Tuesday, we’ll turn this into an SOW and route for signature (we can do DocuSign).

Thanks — Monica Patel
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
(attachment: sla-redlines-fluxbank-20261115.pdf)

Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -08:00
From: Ava Lind <ava.lind@fluxbank.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Subject: Re: Proposed technical guardrails and SLOs for pilot — commercial terms

Monica / team — thanks. We’ll send the redlines and the two route IDs by COB Tuesday. We appreciate the p99 concession and the runbook commitment; if the pilot performs as expected we’re prepared to move the renewal to a committed 12-month Dedicated agreement.

Ava
Head of Platform, FluxBank
